question: Who was Ibn Turka?
proposition: Ibn Turka was a mystic with lettrist concerns, wrongly captured by the label 'Spinoza of Iran'.
scholar: ʿAbd al-Ḥusayn Zarrīnkūb (as reported by Melvin-Koushki)
reasoning: MK reports only that Zarrinkub objects to the 'Spinoza of Iran' title as misrepresentative of Ibn Turka's 'more mystical and lettrist concerns' (pdf p.24 n.17); his own account of Ibn Turka is not given on these pages.
So the reading has a lettrist element MK does not dispute; the point of difference is that it stays within mysticism. MK does not answer Zarrinkub directly on the page.

MK is a partisan reporter and this is one footnote: the reconstruction is thin. Confidence records how fully the pages of MK's dissertation let us reconstruct this position and its grounds, not whether it is true.
